question: Which conversion laws share an owner across formats, and what Markdown reuse contract preserves every partial-prefix result without repeated whole-response work?
trigger: The owner asked for a best-api-review audit of every open ledger unit, judged afresh because earlier verdicts came from a weaker model, then widened it on 2026-10-04 to every existing ledger item. It asked for verdicts only, so no plan, build or panel follows in this run. This scope was closed, with a latest pursue verdict, at queue position 30. It is not the unit next returned, which was reads.
requirements: Shared conversion laws (URL role safety, loss severity, emission claims) keep one private owner each; syntax stays with each format owner.
Streaming Markdown reuses converted segments through parseSlice({ previous }) and equals a fresh parse of every prefix, diagnostics included.
Every read of a rendered document observes one immutable document without editing the source editor.
Input a mapping cannot represent is a diagnosed refusal under lossPolicy; content loss follows the policy and property loss warns.
When a matched capability exists, the same source structure maps to the same Plate representation across formats instead of being judged by one format's limits.
evidenceReuse: Reused the 2026-09-29 static-read review, the static-document-rendering execution, the conversion-boundary decision page and the proportional-cost plan's named HTML limits as history. Rechecked on the live tree the parseSlice previous contract and reuse guard in MarkdownPlugin.ts, readsDocument on BaseTocPlugin and PlateStatic, html-unsupported-content reporting in HtmlPlugin.ts, isHtmlBlockElement, and the List plugin's HTML prepareDocument and Markdown list decoder. Confirmed by git log that no commit since 2026-09-30 touched the List HTML decode. No probe was run, so the merge behavior is read from source.
summary: The job is one owner per cross-format conversion law (URL role safety, loss severity, emission claims) and a Markdown streaming contract that equals a fresh parse of every prefix without whole-response work. Live source holds the adopted target. parseSlice({ previous }) reuses converted segments, Plite createEditorView(editor, { document }) binds every read of a rendered document, HTML encoders claim what they write and report html-unsupported-content, and render.readsDocument drives static reuse. The remaining material gap is HTML list import. The List HTML mapping's prepareDocument unwraps every block child of an li that holds more than one block (or one paragraph) into the item's inline content, so paragraphs merge, a code block or table loses its structure, and no claim or diagnostic records it. Markdown decodes the same list item's later blocks as separate blocks at indent + 1 without listType, so a matched representation exists. The decision page and the proportional-cost plan list this, the unreported table list properties and the subtree-wide decoder claims as open limits with no owner. Reopening the parser, the previous-result contract or a universal codec has no new evidence, and the repair is a bounded fix at the List HTML mapping.

Owner: the List plugin's HTML mapping (prepareDocument and decode); no public API change.

reconciliation.question: Which conversion laws share an owner across formats, and what Markdown reuse contract preserves every partial-prefix result without repeated whole-response work?
reconciliation.reason: Document views, HTML emission claims and static reuse hold in live source; its HTML accounting covered serialization claims, and the parse-side list merge sits outside what it proved.

alternatives: Keeping the current design and closing the scope loses. The adopted laws hold, but a silent structural merge on HTML list import contradicts the content-loss law the program adopted, and its known limits have no owner.

Reporting the flattening as a lossy warning and keeping the merge is partial. It ends the silence but still discards structure that Plate can represent, since Markdown already maps the same item to continuation blocks.

Decoding an li's later blocks as continuation blocks (indent + 1, no listType), as the Markdown list decoder does, and reporting only what stays unrepresentable, including list properties a table cannot carry, is the lane to pursue, inside the List plugin's HTML mapping with no new public API.
Moving list topology into a shared private helper that both the Markdown and HTML list mappings use is a candidate inside the fix, and the owner stays the List plugin, not a format-neutral codec.
Routing HTML lists through MDAST or a universal codec is rejected again. HTML and Markdown syntax stay distinct, and the defect is one mapping's preparation step.
Reopen parseSlice({ previous }), the parser engine or static document views: Stop. Live source matches the adopted contract and no contradicting evidence exists.
